properties.title: DALE-CT: Depth-Aware 2D Slice Encoders Learn an Anatomical World Model of Chest CT
properties.membership_rationale: The inspected implementation learns anatomical representations but does not advance persistent state through a learned successor transition.

properties.review_access: Full supplied text and earlier automated page-image review notes.

properties.design: Representation pretraining, matched spatial-sampling ablation, frozen anatomical/diagnostic probes, external transfer and preprocessing experiments.
properties.shared_assertion_contract: Assertions on study:B005 scoped to use:B005 describe common inspected properties of these seven configurations. Explicit model_version_id scopes override this common scope. Shared assertions do not imply shared weights, identical performance or inheritance of another configuration's results.
properties.coordinate: Cranio-caudal spatial position within acquired CT, not elapsed clinical time.
properties.world_relevance: Thoracic organ anatomy; no modelsWorld relation is asserted because an evolving organ-world mechanism is not implemented.

properties.purpose: Offline chest-CT representation research and current-observation diagnostic/anatomical probing.
properties.population: Acquired human chest CT; detailed clinical eligibility and demographics insufficiently reported.
properties.user: Medical imaging research community; no evaluated clinical workflow.
properties.decision_boundary: No therapeutic, acquisition or robotic action selection/execution.

properties.name: DALE-CT-0
properties.objective: LeJEPA invariance plus SIGReg, without auxiliary head.
properties.sampling: 12 mm slabs; ReX/TS annotation-guided local crops.

properties.name: DALE-CT-1S-v2
properties.objective: LeJEPA/SIGReg plus dense CLS/patch supervision over 118 TS classes; ReX auxiliary terms inert.
properties.distinct_from: Earlier patch-14, CLS-only DALE-CT-1S used in cited report-generation work.

properties.name: DALE-CT-2S
properties.objective: LeJEPA/SIGReg plus weighted BCE over 118 TS and 14 ReX CLS/patch coverage targets.

properties.name: DALE-CT-0-L
properties.objective: LeJEPA invariance plus SIGReg; no auxiliary head.
properties.sampling: Three-slice native-z slabs; TS-guided local crops; no ReX guidance.
properties.scale_boundary: Corpus, slab, guidance, normalization and optimization change together.

properties.name: Depth-aware ViT-Base ablation
properties.objective: LeJEPA across 12 mm slabs; no auxiliary head.
properties.matched_factors: Architecture, initialization, corpus and budget, as reported.

properties.name: Pure-2D ViT-Base ablation
properties.objective: LeJEPA with intra-slice views; no auxiliary head.
properties.interpretation: Informative static representation control; lower shared-basis continuity does not establish absence of anatomical information.

properties.name: Finetuned DINOv2
properties.architecture: Natural-image-initialized ViT-Large with Registers, adapted to single-channel CT.
properties.training: CT-RATE continual pretraining using DINO-MX momentum-teacher distillation and iBOT masked modeling.
properties.comparison_boundary: Initialization, objective, global resolution and local-crop composition differ from DALE-CT.

properties.semantics: Separate encoder-plus-probe configurations, not an ensemble or simultaneous composition of all encoders.
properties.flow: HU preprocessing → acquired-slice encoding → pooling/projection → current-observation readout.
CT preprocessing → frozen scaled encoder → fitted current-observation probes.
properties.readiness_boundary: Probe partitions are reported; full independence from multisource pretraining remains unresolved.

properties.split_statement: Patient-disjoint splits stated in release description.
properties.count_boundary: Scans are not equated with unique patients.

properties.protocol: Frozen encoders; validation AUPRC selects pooling/rate; validation fits classwise F1 thresholds.
properties.reporting: Table VI single selected probe; 2,000-resample test bootstrap.

properties.tasks: Observed-slice continuity, position decoding, ordering and residual organ clustering.
properties.additional_clustering_result: DALE-CT-2S NMI/ARI is separately reported in Section V-D.

properties.reporting: Available-seed mean, 1–5 per model; exact per-arm counts unreported.

evidence_fragments.content:
DALE-CT: Depth-Aware 2D Slice Encoders Learn
an Anatomical World Model of Chest CT
Evan W. Damron, Mahmut S. Gokmen, Mitchell A. Klusty, Caroline N. Leach, Emily B. Collier,
V . K. Cody Bumgardner

We use the term in
this passive sense, with the cranio-caudal axis of a CT volume
playing the role the temporal axis plays in video: slices are
successive states, and depth-aware training asks the encoder
to relate them.

Our foundational models are initialized from scratch and
trained with LeJEPA [5], which pairs a multi-crop invariance
objective with SIGReg. Unlike teacher–student frameworks,
LeJEPA routes every view through a single symmetric encoder
fθ followed by a projection headg ϕ, with no momentum
encoder, predictor, or stop-gradient. Although the models
remain native 2D-slice encoders, the multi-crop views are
sampled across the depth of a 3D slab composed of multiple
slices (Section III-C); routing physically displaced, multi-scale
views through the unified encoder encourages the network
to learn cross-slice anatomical consistency rather than strictly
intra-slice features.

•DALE-CT-0:the LeJEPA objective alone, no auxiliary
head (λ aux = 0).
•DALE-CT-1S-v2:a single-source (1S) auxiliary head
over the 118 TotalSegmentator classes, applied densely
to both the[CLS]and patch tokens; ReXGroundingCT
is held inert, isolating the TS objective against the 2S
model.
•DALE-CT-2S:a dual-source (2S) head over the 118 TS
and 14 ReX classes jointly.
The auxiliary head is a pair of linear layers mapping the
backbone feature dimension to the TS and ReX class counts.
For every crop, both the global[CLS]token and the patch
tokens are supervised, so each crop contributes a CLS-level
and a patch-level prediction. Targets are dense fractional
coverage: for TS, masks are one-hot over 118 classes; for
ReX, binary abnormality channels are binarized per pixel and
restricted to scans carrying ReX annotations. Coverage is the
mean over the crop and the average-pool over the patch grid,
yielding continuous targets in[0,1]for both sources.

For
the CT-RATE models the preferred guidance label is a ReX
abnormality mask when present; DALE-CT-0-L disables ReX
guidance entirely, as the multi-source pool lacks ReX labels
outside CT-RATE, and guides local crops on TS foreground
alone.

A ViT-
Large with Registers, initialized from natural-image weights,
is continually pretrained on CT-RATE via DINO-MX [30],
combining DINO distillation from a momentum teacher with
iBOT masked image modeling; we benchmark the result as
Finetuned DINOv2. The two paradigms differ in how they sta-
bilize learning: DINOv2 relies on a teacher–student asymmetry
with stop-gradients, whereas LeJEPA uses a symmetric joint-
embedding objective with an isotropic-Gaussian regularizer.

an 80/20 patient-level split of
the 3,002-scan CT-RATE validation set (593 test scans).

we replace each encoder’s native aggregation with a trained
head, search a grid of learning rates and pooling schemes
(average, max, and learned-attention), feed the pooled vector
to a linear layer over the 18 CT-RATE abnormalities, select
the best probe by validation AUPRC, and fit per-class F1-
maximizing decision thresholds on the validation set. All mod-
els are evaluated on a common CT-RATE partition (4,942 train
/ 992 test scans), and we report 95% confidence intervals from
a 2,000-resample test-set bootstrap.

probes predict the 14 ReX abnormality classes or the 118
TS coverage classes, and patch-level probes predict the corre-
sponding masks pooled to the ViT patch grid;

Note: All models are probed by us on the common RAD-ChestCT test set (Section V-B); each value is the mean over the available probe seeds (1–5 per
model) with a 95% bootstrap CI on that mean in gray. Bold marks the best overall model per column; underline marks the best DALE-CT model per
column. “Frozen” applies the CT-RATE-trained classifier directly to RAD-ChestCT; “Retrained” keeps the encoder frozen and trains a new classifier on the
RAD-ChestCT train split. Frozen-arm Macro F1 is threshold-sensitive on RAD-ChestCT’s small validation set and should be read alongside AUPRC/AUROC.

We are careful not to over-claim the25k→287k contrast as a
controlled scaling law. DALE-CT-0-L differs from the released
DALE-CT-0 along several axes simultaneously (Table VIII,
Appendix B): corpus (multi-source vs. CT-RATE), slab instan-
tiation (3-slice native-z 1 vs. 12 mm physical), ReX guidance
(absent vs.0.8), normalization statistics (fit to the full pool
vs. CT-RATE, via the identical 0.5/99.5-percentile procedure),
and schedule (3 epochs / 191k iterations / batch 384 on 16
H100s vs. 50k iterations / batch 512 on 8 H200s). The contrast
therefore reflects the full configuration of a broader-corpus
instantiation, not corpus size in isolation.

Because our two frozen probes did not translate
that geometry into higher downstream accuracy, we present
the world model as a property of the representation and
establish performance separately in a head-to-head frozen-
probe benchmark.

To support open science and reproducibility, all training
code, evaluation pipelines, and pretrained model weights dis-
cussed in this work are publicly available. The core train-
ing framework and LeJEPA implementation are available in
theDALE-CT repository. The head-to-head evaluation har-
ness is released separately as thechest-ct-foundation-model-
benchmarkrepository, which distributes the unified backbone
loader that normalizes every evaluated encoder behind one
interface, the patient-disjoint splits, the frozen-probe protocol,
and every benchmark result reported here. The benchmark is
maintained as a living resource and continues to add encoders
beyond those evaluated in this paper; the numbers reported
here correspond to a fixed snapshot of its results.

All pretrained weights are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub
under CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0

All DALE-CT variants use a ViT-Large, patch-16 backbone
initialized from scratch and trained with Distributed Data

3D MIL probing (Section V-B).The grid search spans six
learning rates ({0.3,0.1,0.03,0.01,0.003,0.001}) and three
pooling schemes (average, max, and learned-attention, a subset
of the five in [2]). The pooled vector feeds a linear layer over
the 18 CT-RATE abnormalities, optimized for 15,000 steps
with SGD (batch 16, momentum 0.95, weight decay 0, cosine
annealing). The best probe is selected by validation AUPRC,
followed by a per-class F1-maximizing decision threshold fit
on the validation set.
Token aggregation and uncertainty.The 3D baselines
contribute a flattened grid of volumetric tokens from a cen-
tered crop, and the 2D models contribute a per-slice[CLS]
token bag; average, max, and learned-attention pooling reduce
either to a single vector.

Both the probe and its ground
truth derive from TotalSegmentator, so the span results speak
to inference cost rather than accuracy against an independent
reference.

On the 414-scan ReX-annotated split,
a ridge regressor (regularization selected by cross-validation
over10 −3–103) is fit on the training scans from per-slice
[CLS]embeddings to normalized within-scan positionz∈
[0,1]; its weight vector defines the dominant linear position
direction, and each test-scan embedding is residualized by
projecting out this single direction.

legacy_cells.B: DALE-CT: Depth-Aware 2D Slice Encoders Learn an Anatomical World Model of Chest CT
legacy_cells.C: Damron, Evan W., Gokmen, Mahmut S., Klusty, Mitchell A., Leach, Caroline N., Collier, Emily B., Bumgardner, V. K. Cody
legacy_cells.S: Do depth-aware CT-slice representations encode anatomical order and content, and how do frozen features perform on thoracic-abnormality classification?
legacy_cells.AI: Chest CT volumes and axial 2D slices sampled from volumes
legacy_cells.AJ: ViT-Large patch-16; ViT-Base for matched sampling ablation; ViT-Large with Registers for DINOv2 baseline
legacy_cells.AK: DALE-CT models trained from scratch; DINOv2 comparison baseline initialized from natural-image weights
legacy_cells.AL: LeJEPA multi-crop invariance plus SIGReg; optional dense auxiliary supervision
legacy_cells.AZ: Frozen embedding geometry visualized by PCA; slice position, slice order, and organ identity probed from embeddings
legacy_cells.BV: LLeJEPA=(1−λ)Linv+λLSIGReg (λ=0.02); optional weighted BCE auxiliary losses (λaux=0.1)
legacy_cells.BX: CT-RATE pretraining: 25,692 chest CTs; scaled DALE-CT-0-L: 287,302 scans from 32 collections
legacy_cells.CA: DALE-CT-0/2S: 50,000 iterations on 8 H200 GPUs; DALE-CT-1S-v2: 66,667 iterations on 8 H100 GPUs; DALE-CT-0-L: 3 epochs, 191,357 iterations, batch 384 on 16 H100 GPUs
legacy_cells.DN: CT-RATE; RAD-ChestCT; National Lung Screening Trial (NLST); multi-source chest-CT pool
legacy_cells.DQ: CT-RATE pretraining: 25,692 scans; multi-source pretraining: 287,302 training scans; CT-RATE test: 992 scans; RAD-ChestCT test: 360 scans
legacy_cells.FL: A shared 2D ViT-L/16 encoder and projector embed multi-crop views from neighboring CT slices; optional auxiliary linear heads predict dense TS/ReX labels. No patient-temporal transition model or planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces DALE-CT depth-aware 2D slice encoders trained with LeJEPA; studies anatomical latent continuity, auxiliary anatomical/abnormality supervision, frozen-probe performance, and scale-up to a 287k-scan corpus.
legacy_cells.FN: Depth-aware sampling raised Latent Continuity Score from 0.4263 to 1.6844 versus pure-2D sampling, while classification was nearly unchanged; DALE-CT-2S reached CT-RATE AUROC 0.8247 and scaled DALE-CT-0-L reached RAD-ChestCT retrained AUROC 0.7572.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors state that their frozen probes did not translate the geometry into higher downstream accuracy; only two simple frozen probes were tested, leaving benefits in advanced aggregation pipelines unresolved.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors leave for future work whether smoother, better-ordered embeddings help advanced MIL aggregation and report-generation pipelines.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that, to their knowledge, no prior CT foundation model framed frozen representations as an anatomical world model.
legacy_cells.FR: The demonstrated result is anatomical representation geometry across spatial CT slices, not evolving patient physiology: no learned patient-time transition, treatment/action-conditioned outcome, multi-step rollout, causal identification, or planning result is shown. The authors explicitly describe their use as passive and spatial.
